Simulated adult NCD survey (STEPS-style)

Source: R/data.R
ncd_survey.Rd

A simulated nationally representative-style survey of adults aged 18-69, drawn from a known synthetic population by stratified two-stage cluster sampling. It mimics the structure of WHO STEPS and DHS microdata (strata, primary sampling units, unequal sampling weights, raw response codes with "don't know" answers) so that every function in the package can be demonstrated. The data are entirely synthetic; regions are fictitious and no estimate describes any real country.

Usage

ncd_survey

Format

A data frame with 2,400 rows (one adult per household) and 18 variables:

hh_id

Household identifier (links to child_anthro).

region

Region (6 fictitious regions, "Region A" to "Region F").

residence

"Urban" or "Rural".

stratum

Sampling stratum (region x residence, 12 strata).

psu

Primary sampling unit (enumeration area), 120 in total.

wt

Sampling weight, normalised to mean 1 (as in DHS).

sex

"Female" or "Male".

age

Age in completed years (18-69).

wealth_score

Continuous household wealth index (higher = richer).

wealth_quintile

Weighted wealth quintile, 1 (poorest) to 5 (richest).

bmi

Body mass index (kg/m^2).

htn_raw, dm_raw, arth_raw, asthma_raw, angina_raw, stroke_raw

Raw answers to "Has a doctor or health worker ever told you that you have hypertension / diabetes / arthritis / asthma / angina or heart disease / stroke?", coded 1 = yes, 2 = no, 9 = don't know.

dep_raw

Raw answer for depression, coded as text: "Yes", "No", "Don't know".

Source

Simulated; see data-raw/simulate_survey.R in https://github.com/StatAid-Research-Lab/SurveyNCD.

Details

The population has 6 regions of unequal size, each divided into urban and rural enumeration areas (12 strata). Ten enumeration areas were selected by simple random sampling in every stratum and 20 households in each, so small regions and urban areas are over-sampled and the weights vary about 15-fold. The code that generates the population and the sample is in data-raw/ in the package source repository.

See also

child_anthro

Examples

head(ncd_survey)
#>   hh_id   region residence          stratum psu       wt    sex age
#> 1   908 Region A     Urban Region A - Urban   1 1.287859   Male  26
#> 2   932 Region A     Urban Region A - Urban   1 1.287859   Male  25
#> 3   936 Region A     Urban Region A - Urban   1 1.287859   Male  35
#> 4   937 Region A     Urban Region A - Urban   1 1.287859   Male  28
#> 5   938 Region A     Urban Region A - Urban   1 1.287859 Female  41
#> 6   939 Region A     Urban Region A - Urban   1 1.287859   Male  38
#>   wealth_score wealth_quintile  bmi htn_raw dm_raw arth_raw asthma_raw
#> 1        0.926               4 17.3       2      2        2          2
#> 2       -0.162               2 25.8       2      9        2          2
#> 3       -0.477               2 20.7       2      2        2          2
#> 4        1.607               5 24.4       2      2        2          2
#> 5        0.353               3 24.8       2      2        2          2
#> 6        1.297               4 25.5       1      2        2          2
#>   angina_raw stroke_raw    dep_raw
#> 1          2          2         No
#> 2          2          9         No
#> 3          2          2         No
#> 4          2          2         No
#> 5          2          2 Don't know
#> 6          2          2         No
ncd_survey$htn <- recode_binary(ncd_survey$htn_raw, yes = 1, no = 2)
#> Warning: Some values matched neither `yes` nor `no`; leaving them as NA.
